newsitem.title: USA: James Earl Ray again in critical condition.
newsitem.headline: James Earl Ray again in critical condition.

text.p: James Earl Ray, convicted assassin of civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., was reported in critical condition Thursday in another reversal in his battle with terminal liver disease.

Columbia Nashville Memorial Hospital said Ray, 69, was re-admitted there Wednesday night and was in critical condition. He was in the same facility earlier in the week but had been taken back to the prison where he is serving a 99-year sentence.
A judge in Memphis, meanwhile, has scheduled a hearing on May 6 to decide when and where the rifle Ray allegedly used to kill King 29 years ago will be test fired.

Ray confessed to killing King but later denied it, and has been trying to re-open the case and win a trial. His lawyers contend that tests on the gun would justify a trial by showing it was not the murder weapon.

The rifle was found tossed in the doorway of a shop near the Memphis motel where King was shot. Ray's lawyers have said it was a "throw down" gun and not the actual murder weapon and that Ray was only a pawn in a larger plot to kill King.
Previous test firings on the rifle by the FBI and by congressional investigators were not conclusive. King's family has backed Ray's request for a trial.
Ray has been in and our of the same hospital repeatedly since last last year. His lawyers have urged that the gun test and new trial issues be decided quickly because he does not have long to live.
